title: Affine-local characterization of flat families with geometric complete-intersection fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For a field $k$, say a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ if it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras which are local complete intersections in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; the empty scheme is allowed. The following conditions are equivalent. (1) The morphism $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] its geometric fibre, the fibre product $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [def-weil-geometric-fibre], is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. (2) For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ and every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, the induced map $A\to B$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. (3) There exist an affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_a V_a$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, and for each $a$ an affine open cover $f^{-1}(V_a)=\bigcup_b U_{ab}$, $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{ab}$, such that each induced map $A_a\to B_{ab}$ is flat and of finite presentation and every fibre ring $B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A_a$.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), conditions (1), (2), (4); Tag 01UC (definition-syntomic); Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic) and Tag 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres). Ring syntomicity is precisely the three written ring conditions by Algebra Tag 00SL (definition-lci). The geometric-fibre formulation uses Algebra Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), algebra.tex, and Morphisms lemma-local-complete-intersection.

proof.text: Assume (1). On every affine pair, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] gives flatness and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives finite presentation. For $\mathfrak p\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1) gives finite presentation of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_A B$. The symmetry $c\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes c$, inverse $b\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes b$, identifies this with $S=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The finitely many variable images in a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] generate $S$, proving finite type.

source.place: Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), (1) implies (2), and 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) implies (2); Algebra Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), (4).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak p$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. It gives a geometric point through $V$ by [def-weil-geometric-point]. Condition (1) supplies its complete-intersection fibre cover; step 1 supplies finite type of $S$. Apply [lem-trf-lci-geometric-chart-descent] with $K=\Omega$. It gives that $S$ is lci. Together with step 1 this proves (2).

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), descent/ascent; schemes.tex Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product) and 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection). Explicit affine-chart and balanced-tensor comparison extracted from the proof of lem-trf-syntomic-geometric-fibres-affine-criterion, original steps 1, 3 and 6.

proof.text: For (2)$\Rightarrow$(3), choose affine opens $V_a$ covering $Y$ and affine opens $U_{ab}$ covering each open subscheme $f^{-1}(V_a)$, using the local affine property [def-pc-scheme]. Each $U_{ab}$ is also open in $X$ and maps into $V_a$, so (2) gives every required ring condition. Empty inverse images permit empty covers.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), (2) implies (4), with ring syntomicity expanded as Algebra Tag 00SL (definition-lci).

proof.text: Assume (3). Given $x\in X$, choose $a$ with $f(x)\in V_a$, then $b$ with $x\in U_{ab}$. The chart morphism $U_{ab}\to V_a$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Restricting to open neighbourhoods identifies its stalk map with $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so this map is flat. Thus [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of $f$. The same affine pair has a finitely presented coordinate map by (3), witnessing finite presentation at $x$ by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. This holds at every point.

source.place: Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize) and 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), the covering-to-pointwise directions written from the definitions.

proof.text: For (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), fix $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ and choose $V_a$ containing its image $y$. By [def-weil-geometric-point] this point factors through $\kappa(y)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Each $S_b=B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is lci by (3), hence finite type by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Apply [lem-trf-lci-residue-chart-cover-extension] to $(U_{ab})_b$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\Omega$. Its hypotheses now hold, and its conclusion gives an lci affine cover of the entire geometric fibre and local finite type. Together with step 4 this proves (1).

lean.statement: theorem syntomic_geometric_fibres_affine_criterion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ((Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (ybar : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y), IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOver Ω (Limits.pullback f ybar) (Limits.pullback.snd f ybar)) ↔ (∀ (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), IsSyntomicAffineChart f V U hUV)) ∧ ((∀ (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), IsSyntomicAffineChart f V U hUV) ↔ (∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Y.Opens), (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i)) ∧ (∀ y : Y, ∃ i, y ∈ V i) ∧ ∀ i, ∃ (J : Type u) (U : J → X.Opens), (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (U j)) ∧ (∀ x : X, x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V i → ∃ j, x ∈ U j) ∧ ∀ j, ∃ hUV : U j ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V i, IsSyntomicAffineChart f (V i) (U j) hUV))
